title: Messi lifts the trophy
timeline: Lionel Messi enters his fifth and, he says beforehand, likely final World Cup.
He plays the tournament of his life: a semi-final masterclass against Croatia, two goals in the final.
After Argentina survive France's Mbappé-inspired comeback, Messi scores in the shootout.
He is handed a bisht robe by the Emir of Qatar before lifting the trophy, an image that circles the world.

title: The Hand of God
timeline: England meet Argentina in a politically charged quarter-final, a year after the Falklands War.
Six minutes into the second half, Diego Maradona punches the ball into the net, going unseen by the referee.
Four minutes later he collects the ball in his own half and dribbles past five England players to score again.
Maradona later calls the first goal 'a little bit the hand of God, a little bit the head of Maradona'.

title: The Maracanazo
timeline: Brazil enter the final match of the 1950 group stage needing only a draw against Uruguay.
Newspapers had already printed pre-match editions celebrating a Brazilian championship.
Uruguay come from behind to win 2-1 in front of the largest crowd ever to watch a football match.
The defeat is still described in Brazil as a national trauma.

title: Zidane's headbutt
tagline: A legend's last kick, and no kick at all
timeline: Zinedine Zidane opens the scoring in his final match with a panenka penalty.
Italy's Marco Materazzi equalises and, moments later, exchanges words with Zidane.
Zidane headbutts Materazzi in the chest and is sent off in extra time.
France go on to lose the final on penalties, and Zidane's career ends mid-pitch rather than with the trophy.

title: Geoff Hurst's hat-trick
tagline: Still the only one in a final
timeline: West Germany equalise deep into stoppage time to send the final to extra time.
Geoff Hurst's shot cannons down off the crossbar; the goal is awarded despite lasting debate over whether it crossed the line.
Hurst scores again in the closing seconds as fans spill onto the pitch.
It remains the only hat-trick scored in a World Cup final.

title: Pelé's arrival
timeline: Pelé makes his World Cup debut at 17, the youngest player in the tournament's history to that point.
He scores a hat-trick in the semi-final against France.
In the final against Sweden he scores twice, including a goal where he chests the ball over a defender before volleying it in.
He becomes the youngest player ever to win a World Cup.

title: Iniesta's late winner
tagline: Spain's first title, in the 116th minute
timeline: Spain and the Netherlands play a tense, foul-heavy final that stays scoreless through 90 minutes.
Extra time brings a Dutch red card and mounting pressure from Spain's possession game.
In the 116th minute, Andrés Iniesta controls a chested pass and volleys past the Dutch keeper.
Spain win their first World Cup, and Iniesta's shirt afterward reads a tribute to a friend who had recently died.

title: Mbappé's final hat-trick
timeline: Down 2-0 with France going through the motions, Kylian Mbappé converts a penalty in the 80th minute.
He scores again 97 seconds later with a first-time volley to level the final at 2-2.
He completes his hat-trick in extra time, only the second in a World Cup final.
Despite the effort, France lose the shootout and Mbappé finishes the tournament as top scorer.

title: Cameroon shock Argentina
timeline: Defending champions Argentina, with Diego Maradona, open the tournament against Cameroon.
Cameroon play with two men sent off yet still find a late winner.
Francois Omam-Biyik's header stuns the champions 1-0.
Cameroon go on to reach the quarter-finals, then a first for an African nation.

title: Senegal beat the champions
timeline: Senegal, playing their first ever World Cup, face defending champions France in the opening match.
Papa Bouba Diop scores the only goal and is mobbed by teammates in a celebratory dance around the corner flag.
France go on to be eliminated in the group stage without scoring a single goal.
Senegal reach the quarter-finals in their debut tournament.

title: USA shock England
tagline: The result English papers assumed was a typo
timeline: England, playing their first World Cup, are heavy favourites against a part-time USA squad.
Joe Gaetjens, a Haitian-born dishwasher playing amateur football in New York, heads in the only goal.
Some English newspapers reportedly assumed the wire-service scoreline was a misprint for 10-1.
It remains one of the biggest upsets in World Cup history.

title: Carlos Alberto's team goal
timeline: In the 1970 final, Brazil work the ball through several players with one-touch passing.
Pelé receives it near the box and, without looking up, rolls it wide to an overlapping run.
Captain Carlos Alberto arrives at full speed to drive it into the corner.
The goal is widely cited as one of the greatest team goals in football history.
